exposure: Neonatal demographic characteristics (sex, birth weight, gestational age)
Clinical features of sepsis (early vs. late onset)
outcome: Blood culture-positive sepsis characteristics (clinical, epidemiological, pathogen identification)
cohort: A total of 227 neonates with clinical signs of sepsis admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in central India.
finding: The study revealed a predominance of late-onset sepsis in neonates at the NICU, with Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus as key multidrug-resistant pathogens, and significant associations between low birth weight/preterm birth and increased sepsis incidence.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was present in 70.5% of the neonates.
gest_age: Preterm birth was identified as a significant factor associated with increased incidence of sepsis.
